title: An operational guide to resin 3D printing of geological macromodels
author: Idris, Seers, et al.

steps.title: Level build plate
steps.instruction: Ensure the build plate is level with the LCD screen before any printing begins.

steps.title: Secure and fill resin vat
steps.instruction: Attach the resin vat/reservoir to the printer and fill it with resin up to the designated fill line.

steps.title: Prepare resin
steps.instruction: Gently shake the resin bottle, avoiding vigorous agitation, then pour the resin into the vat and let it sit for several minutes to allow bubbles to dissipate.

steps.title: Set printer parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the AnyCubic PhotonMonoX with the following settings: layer thickness 0.05 mm; normal exposure 2 s; bottom exposure 40 s; bottom layers 6; Z‑lift speed 2 mm/s; Z‑lift distance 8 mm.

steps.title: Load sliced model
steps.instruction: Insert the USB flash drive containing the sliced model, select the file on the touchscreen, and start the print.

steps.title: Allow post‑print drainage
steps.instruction: When the print finishes, keep the model attached to the build plate for several minutes so excess resin can drain back into the vat.

steps.title: Remove model from plate
steps.instruction: Using a plastic spatula (avoid steel), gently pry the model off the build plate; if adhesion is strong, pour hot water along the contact points to loosen it.

steps.title: Clean work area
steps.instruction: Wipe the build plate and surrounding area with a paper towel and isopropyl alcohol (IPA).

steps.title: Remove supports
steps.instruction: Break off support structures by hand within the first few hours; use wire cutters only if necessary.

steps.title: Wash model
steps.instruction: Submerge the printed model in a container of IPA to remove residual resin; for highly tortuous pores, optionally use a sonic bath with cleaning agent or flush the pores with a syringe.

steps.title: Cure model
steps.instruction: Expose the washed model to direct sunlight for approximately 30 minutes, or place it in a dedicated wash‑and‑cure station.

steps.title: Seal drain holes
steps.instruction: Apply hot‑glue from a hot glue gun to any drain holes to create a watertight seal.

steps.title: Sand for transparency
steps.instruction: Progressively sand the model with wet sandpaper of increasing grit: 400 → 600 → 800 → 1500 grit.

steps.title: Polish surface
steps.instruction: Using a polishing disk attached to a rotary multitool or bench‑top grinder, polish the sanded areas with polishing compound to achieve a clear finish, especially on the coverslip region.

steps.title: Thread inlet/outlet ports
steps.instruction: Tap the inlet and outlet ports with a 10‑32 tap using a tap wrench to create threads for PEEK fittings.

steps.title: Connect fluid lines
steps.instruction: Attach a syringe pump to the inlet via a standard 1/16 inch PEEK flow line and connect the outlet to a drainage container with a matching PEEK line.

steps.title: Set up imaging station
steps.instruction: Place the assembled macromodel on a light pad directly beneath a digital camera mounted on a copy stand for nadir‑view recording of flooding experiments.
